title.narrative: Increased capacity of national institutions to fight against child labour in Nigeria

description.narrative:
Child labour deprives children of their childhood, their potential, and their dignity. It harms children mentally, physically, socially, and morally. It interferes with their schooling, preventing them from attending or concentrating in school. In the most serious cases, it may involve children being separated from their families, exposed to serious hazards, or enslaved. In Nigeria, the 2022 child labour survey report states that there are about 24.6m children in child labour and there are many factors responsible for incidents of child labour. The ILO is implementing projects supporting the government of Nigeria and the social partners to reform legislation and regulations, empowering communities to address child labour and advancing social protection for vulnerable families.
The interventions focus on developing capacities at national, sub-national and local levels to address the root causes of child labour, foster access to education and social protection to vulnerable children and families. In addition, ILO promoting OSH and protecting rights at work for children within working age
